description: At Veracyte, we offer exciting career opportunities for those interested in joining a pioneering team that is committed to transforming cancer care for patients across the globe. Working at Veracyte enables our employees to not only make a meaningful impact on the lives of patients, but to also learn and grow within a purpose driven environment. This is what we call the Veracyte way – it’s about how we work together, guided by our values, to give clinicians the insights they need to help patients make life-changing decisions. Our Values: We Seek A Better Way: We pursue bold ideas, embrace complexity, and keep pushing forward. We Make It Happen: We act with urgency, deliver with excellence, and always find a way. We Are Stronger Together: We engage with empathy, align around what's best for Veracyte, and celebrate as one team. We Care Deeply: We show up with integrity, kindness, and respect for one another. The Position: The Market Access Manager is responsible for the operational infrastructure that enables successful Market Access execution across Veracyte’s diagnostic testing portfolio, including payer credentialing and enrollment, state Medicaid participation, contract implementation, and the system of record for all Market Access agreements and documentation. Reporting to the Director, Market Access & Payer Relations, this individual will partner closely with Market Access, Reimbursement Operations (RCM), external consultants, Client Services, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Regulatory, and Commercial Operations teams to ensure payer contracting and coverage strategies are translated into accurate operational execution. The ideal candidate combines deep knowledge of healthcare reimbursement operations with a proactive, solutions-oriented mindset and a passion for improving patient access to innovative diagnostic testing. Key responsibilities: Lead all payer credentialing, re-credentialing, enrollment, and network participation activities across commercial payers, Medicare contractors, all state Medicaid programs and their associated managed care plans, laboratory benefit managers, and other reimbursement stakeholders. Own the end-to-end lifecycle, including initial applications, revalidation, roster and demographic updates, and ongoing maintenance requirements. Manage state-specific Medicaid enrollment requirements, including out-of-state laboratory enrollment where permitted, documentation and attestations, application fees, risk-level screening obligations such as fingerprinting and site visits, and subsequent contracting with Medicaid managed care plans once state enrollment is active. Manage federal government documentation, including SAM ID and associated opportunities, Federal Supply Schedule changes, FSS applications, and documents related to SBA plans, within required federal timelines. Coordinate ownership, control, and managing employee disclosures required by payer and government enrollment applications, working with Legal, Human Resources, Compliance, and executive leadership to gather and safeguard sensitive information. Maintain accurate laboratory, facility, and organizational records across payer systems and enrollment platforms, including NPPES and PECOS demographic data, NPI and taxonomy assignments, PTAN alignment, W-9 and remittance addresses, and payer directory listings. Partner with Regulatory and Quality to ensure CLIA certification and state clinical laboratory licenses and permits remain current, and align enrollment activities with state licensure prerequisites. Own the contract lifecycle after execution, including effective and termination dates, renewal and notice windows, amendments, and escalation of approaching deadlines to the contracting leads. Establish and maintain the system of record for market access documentation, including executed agreements and amendments, payer medical policies and coverage determinations, payer correspondence, and supporting evidence and dossier materials. Maintain version control, access permissions, and retention standards across document management, Customer Relationship Management (CRM), and Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) platforms. Collaborate with Reimbursement Operations (RCM) teams to identify and resolve enrollment-related claim issues, reimbursement delays, and payer operational challenges, including those involving payer portals such as Availity. Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, process documentation, and operational controls related to enrollment, payer setup, contract administration, and reimbursement operations. Support related payer audits, credentialing reviews, and compliance requests. Select, implement, and administer enrollment tracking and contract repository systems, and manage credentialing vendors, external consultants, and third-party partners. Develop dashboards, reporting, and key performance indicators that measure operational performance, including enrollment cycle time by payer type, percentage of target Medicaid lives with active enrollment, on-time revalidation rate, denial dollars attributable to enrollment or configuration defects, and contract record completeness. Evaluate current workflows, identify opportunities for operational efficiencies, and execute process improvements through the effective use of automation and artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Manage group inboxes for payer correspondence and contracting communications. Who You Are: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. A minimum of 6 – 7 years of experience in healthcare reimbursement operations, payer credentialing, provider enrollment, managed care operations, revenue cycle, market access operations, or a related function. Demonstrated experience managing payer enrollment across both commercial and government payers, including hands-on multi-state Medicaid enrollment and revalidation. Working knowledge of enrollment systems and requirements relevant to facility and laboratory entities, including NPPES, PECOS, state Medicaid provider portals, and enrollment tracking platforms. Demonstrated ownership of a recurring compliance calendar such as revalidation, recredentialing, licensure renewal, or contract renewal, with a track record of preventing lapses. Experience administering contracts, fee schedules, or reimbursement documentation as a system of record, including version control and access management. Strong project management skills, including experience coordinating cross-functional initiatives involving reimbursement, billing, legal, compliance, finance, and commercial teams while managing multiple priorities, deadlines, and stakeholders. Experience developing and maintaining operational documentation, workflows, and standard operating procedures. Ability to manage sensitive personal and corporate information, including ownership and control disclosures, with a high degree of professionalism, accuracy, and confidentiality. Preferred Qualifications Experience supporting molecular diagnostics, genomic testing, laboratory developed tests (LDTs), precision medicine, oncology diagnostics, or other specialty diagnostic products. Experience enrolling an out-of-state laboratory in state Medicaid programs and navigating state-specific restrictions on out-of-state laboratory participation. Experience with Medicaid managed care plan contracting and roster processes as distinct from state fee-for-service enrollment. Experience with credentialing and contracting in VA and DoD facilities. Experience implementing or administering an enrollment tracking platform or contract lifecycle management system. Certified Provider Credentialing Specialist (CPCS) or similar credentialing certification. Familiarity with Medicare coverage, commercial payer operations, laboratory benefit managers, and diagnostic reimbursement pathways. Experience working with healthcare compliance, audit readiness, and credentialing governance processes. #LI-Hybrid The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to years of experience, skillset, geographic location, industry, education, etc. Base pay is one part of the Total Package that is provided to compensate and recognize employees for their work, and this role may be eligible for additional discretionary bonuses/incentives, and restricted stock units. Pay range $100,000—$135,000 USD What We Can Offer You Veracyte is a growing company that offers significant career opportunities if you are curious, driven, patient-oriented and aspire to help us build a great company. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, and are committed to fostering an inclusive workforce, where diverse backgrounds are represented, engaged, and empowered to drive innovative ideas and decisions. We are thrilled to be recognized as a 2024 Certified™ Great Place to Work® in both the US and Israel - a testament to our dynamic, inclusive, and inspiring workplace where passion meets purpose. About Veracyte Veracyte (Nasdaq: VCYT) is a global diagnostics company whose vision is to transform cancer care for patients all over the world. We empower clinicians with the high-value insights they need to guide and assure patients at pivotal moments in the race to diagnose and treat cancer. Our Veracyte Diagnostics Platform delivers high-performing cancer tests that are fueled by broad genomic and clinical data, deep bioinformatic and AI capabilities, and a powerful evidence-generation engine, which ultimately drives durable reimbursement and guideline inclusion for our tests, along with new insights to support continued innovation and pipeline development. For more information, please visit www.veracyte.com or follow us on LinkedIn or X (Twitter). description: Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world. GET TO KNOW US At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. THE OPPORTUNITY We are hiring a Consolidations & Financial Reporting Manager to our Finance team in the United States! Reporting to the Corporate Controller and working closely with our external reporting team, this person will lead the use of AI and automation across our accounting and reporting processes, redesigning how we close, consolidate, report, and document so the work is faster, more automated, and well controlled. A key focus will be supporting the preparation of our quarterly and annual external financial statements and disclosures. The role also supports technical accounting and SOX compliance and owns our global financial consolidation. This is an individual contributor role with no direct reports. YOUR IMPACT Lead AI automation and adoption across accounting and reporting processes: identify high-volume manual work, automate it with AI tools and agents (such as reconciliations, flux analysis, data aggregation, disclosure tie-outs, and first drafts of memos) with appropriate review over AI-generated output, and help the Accounting team adopt these practices. Build, document, and maintain AI-enabled workflows and reporting automation, including in Pigment and NetSuite, and track the time saved and quality improvements they deliver. Support the external reporting team in preparing quarterly and annual financial statements and footnote disclosures, including populating and tying out financial statement tables, maintaining supporting schedules, and coordinating inputs from Accounting, FP&A, and other teams. Prepare supporting analyses for external reporting, such as flux and variance explanations, key metric reconciliations, and disclosure checklists, ensuring internally reported figures reconcile to externally reported results. Support technical accounting by researching accounting questions, preparing recurring memos and analyses (such as capitalized software and impairment assessments), supporting updates to the accounting policy library, and assessing the reporting impact of new accounting standards. Support SOX compliance, including the design, documentation, operation, and remediation of internal controls over financial reporting, partnering with Internal Controls and process owners. Perform independent reviews of financial reporting schedules, disclosures, and reporting packages to maintain appropriate segregation of duties. Lead the monthly, quarterly, and annual global consolidation process across a multinational, multicurrency entity structure, including intercompany eliminations and foreign currency translation. Own lease accounting under ASC 842. Support the accounting integration and system migration of acquired entities. Support debt covenant compliance reporting and coordinate with internal and external auditors on reporting and control requests. Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life wellness. WHO YOU ARE A hands-on, daily user of AI tools such as Gemini, Claude, or ChatGPT, with concrete examples of work you have automated or redesigned with them. Experience building your own AI workflows or agents, for example with Claude Code or Codex, to automate recurring work such as intercompany eliminations, consolidation tie-outs or disclosure checklists is a strong plus. SEC reporting experience, including preparing or supporting quarterly and annual financial statements and footnote disclosures for a public company. Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance; CPA preferred 6+ years of progressive accounting experience, with a combination of Big 4 public accounting and public company industry experience preferred. Strong U.S. GAAP knowledge, including experience researching and documenting accounting conclusions. Working knowledge of SOX 404 and internal control over financial reporting. Hands-on experience with financial consolidations in a multinational, multicurrency environment. Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP; experience with Pigment or similar tools, disclosure management software (such as Workiva or ActiveDisclosure), or SQL/Python a plus. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, and flexibility to work in a fast-growing, exciting, and agile business. We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience with AI tools, SEC reporting, and accounting are mandatory requirements. WHAT WE OFFER YOU With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life. Actual base salary will be dependent on geographic location, relevant experience, skills, qualifications, and/or other job-related factors. Our benefits include: WELLHUB: Free Gold-level membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you. HEALTHCARE: Health, dental, and vision insurance. Access to telehealth, care concierge, and an Employee Assistance Program. FINANCIAL WELLNESS: Plan for your future with 401(k) match, short-term and long-term disability, and life insurance. FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. We offer all employees a one-time reimbursement to set up their home office equipment and a monthly work allowance to help cover the costs of working from home. Our US HQ is in New York City. We are currently set up to hire in California, Colorado, Connecticut, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Massachusetts, Missouri, North Carolina, New Jersey, New Hampshire, New York, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, Virginia, Washington, and Wisconsin. FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE: Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. We offer up to 12 weeks 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. For parents giving birth, we offer up to 18 weeks paid leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while you get settled. CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions, build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here.
